safety_verdicts.content: The pain is described as a constant, progressively worsening burning sensation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No description in Generated Facts of burning quality, constancy, or progressive worsening.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the pain quality/trajectory (constant, burning, progressively worsening) reduces ability to gauge severity and refine the differential (e.g., cystitis vs pyelonephritis vs other abdominal pathology). This can lead to suboptimal triage and monitoring, though it is unlikely by itself to cause major harm if other key red flags are assessed.

safety_verdicts.content: Urinary symptoms include noticing some pink-colored urine, but no frank hematuria or dysuria.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated Facts do not mention pink urine, hematuria, or dysuria.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Pink urine/possible hematuria and absence of dysuria are clinically important for distinguishing cystitis from nephrolithiasis, glomerular disease, or more complicated infection and may change the need for urinalysis, imaging, and escalation. Missing this can delay appropriate evaluation and treatment of potentially significant pathology.
